annotator_note_en: Treated privilege escalation automatically as S:C and used the fact that it was actively exploited as evidence for AC:L. The final 8.8 matches the chosen vector, but the scope-change and attack-complexity bases do not hold. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

Cited CVE-2023-42824 as CoreMedia/S:C/8.8 and CVE-2023-32435 as an IOGraphics local privilege escalation 7.8 as if they were confirmed precedents. In reality the former is Kernel/S:U/7.8 and the latter is WebKit code execution, so the comparison basis was fabricated and the calculation does not hold. T1 criterion: attaching false attributes to real identifiers to build a comparison basis → kept T1 (a single mis-attribution alone would be T2). Refs: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-42824 and https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2023-32435

From a container RCE, assumed without basis a compromise of the host/other services and chose S:C. N/L/L/N/C/H/H/H is 9.9 but was miscomputed as 9.8, and S:U as 7.7 (actual 8.8), so only the GT band matched. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

Treated an application-DB compromise directly as a change of the security authority boundary and computed the S:C vector as 9.8. The true value of N/L/N/N/C/H/H/H is 10.0. Whether Critical is correct and whether the reasoning is correct are judged separately. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

Expanded to S:C merely because the DB engine is a separate component. Executing SQL against the same application DB does not demonstrate a breach of a different security authority boundary, so the basis for 10.0 is insufficient. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

Inferred network attack feasibility from the fact that several Apple OSes are affected and automatically expanded kernel corruption to S:C. The lack of basis for AV:N/PR:N/S:C produced the 10.0 conclusion. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

The vector is correct, but it set the CIA weight to 0.97 or 1 and omitted the subtraction term of the Scope-Changed impact formula, inflating to 10.0. The actual value is 9.1 and only the Critical band matched. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

From an RCE in the current user context, chose S:C without a basis for breaching a different security authority boundary and gave 10.0 with CIA:H. A correct Critical band does not justify the expanded scope basis. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

Lowered a race condition to AC:L and mistook another user session of the same app as a separate Scope. The true value of N/L/L/R/C/H/H/N, 8.7, also does not match the estimated 8.1, so apart from the correct High there is a flaw in the basis. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

Interpreted 'no additional execution privilege needed' as PR:N and expanded kernel privilege escalation to S:C. The true value of L/L/N/N/C/H/H/H, 9.3, does not match the stated 8.4. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

The vector composition is valid, but it mistook the CIA:H weight as 0.97 and rounded 8.27 down to 8.2. The standard L/L/L/N/U/H/H/H is 7.8; a correct High band does not make the wrong calculation valid. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

Used the need to log in as a basis for AV:L and judged CLI→OS command execution directly as S:C. 8.8 matches the chosen vector, but AV and the security authority boundary are wrongly linked. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

From an unverified assumption that the scanner runs as root, linked user→root as S:C. Privilege escalation and a separate security authority boundary are not the same, so the basis for 8.8 does not hold. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

Automatically expanded server code execution from a plugin to S:C and miscomputed N/L/L/N/C/H/H/H as 8.7. The true value of this vector is 9.9 and only the High band matched. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

The vector is correct, but it repeatedly used the constant 8.6 to get 8.83 and rounded down to 8.8. Using the standard constant 8.22 with the roundup rule also coincidentally yields 8.8 — a 'correct answer, wrong calculation' case. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

From a short IPA-statistics description, assumed a user→kernel boundary change and inflated to S:C. The stated L/L/L/N/C/H/H/H is 8.8 and does not match 8.4 either. Even if the GT band is correct, the basis is flawed. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

After recognizing there was no basis for network access, confirmed AV:N merely by assuming 'IPA statistics are usually networked'. It did not demonstrate the exposure path, privilege, or CIA scope from the prompt. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

Made the unfounded generalization that 'OS command execution is usually a Scope change' and miscomputed N/L/L/N/C/H/H/H as 8.7. This vector is 9.9; whether the GT (High) is correct and whether the reasoning is correct are separate. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

The vector L/L/L/N/U/N/N/H is 5.5. Using A:H=0.6 and multiplying by 1.086 for S:U, it produced 6.2, matching only the Medium band. It also arbitrarily lowered the attack-complexity condition. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document

The composition L/L/N/R/U/N/L/N is valid, but it computed the intermediate impact/exploitability values inaccurately and produced 3.2 by ordinary rounding. Applying the standard roundup gives 3.3, and only the Low band matched. Ref: https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document
